title: Mulgore
body: Mulgore is the homeland of the tauren, a sheltered valley of golden grass and gentle hills ringed by mountains on the western edge of the Barrens. The tauren once wandered as nomads, harried by the centaur, until Cairne Bloodhoof, aided by Thrall and his orcs, led his people here, drove the centaur back and claimed the plains. On a towering mesa in the north he raised Thunder Bluff as a refuge for every tribe, and the scattered tribes came together under his rule. Young tauren come of age at Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa and at Bloodhoof Village by Stonebull Lake, proving themselves through the Rites of the Earthmother and the honor of the hunt. Their peace is far from complete. Bristleback quilboar raid from their ravine and even trouble the sacred graves at Red Rocks, Palemane gnolls slaughter the wildlife, Windfury harpies nest along the mountains, dwarves dig into the western hills, and goblins of the Venture Company have poisoned the sacred wells in their hunger for ore.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Mulgore (Warcraft III section: Cairne led the tauren to Mulgore with Thrall's help, centaur driven back, Thunder Bluff founded as a refuge for every tribe, tribes united; enemies of the WoW era)

title: Camp Narache
body: Camp Narache stands at the northern edge of Red Cloud Mesa, high above the plains of southern Mulgore, and here young tauren take their first steps toward adulthood. Chief Hawkwind presides over the camp and reminds every eager newcomer that eagerness is no substitute for wisdom. His son Grull sends novices out to hunt for the tribe's meat, feathers and pelts, while trainers of warriors, hunters, druids and shamans gather in the camp to guide those who follow each path. Seer Ravenfeather readies young shamans for the call of the earth, and the warrior Harutt Thunderhorn teaches that his kind are the ones called upon to defend the borders, hunt the centaur and go to war.

title: Red Cloud Mesa
body: Red Cloud Mesa is a high plateau of rolling grassland atop sheer cliffs in the far south of Mulgore. Plainstriders graze across it, mountain cougars prowl the hills to the south, and battleboars trained by the Bristleback quilboar roam out of the ravine to the east to raid the tauren hunting grounds. A water well lies southeast of Camp Narache, and there Greatmother Hawkwind, the chief's aged mother, goes to draw water at her own unhurried pace. Tucked into the hills directly south of the camp is the abode of Seer Graytongue, who sets young tauren their first test of strength. The mesa is a proving ground, and those who pass its trials follow the road down to Bloodhoof Village.

title: Brambleblade Ravine
body: East of Camp Narache, Brambleblade Ravine is the home of the Bristleback quilboar, who have built a makeshift village there and wage a stubborn war on the tauren from it. Bristleback raiders ambush hunting parties and steal from the camp under cover of darkness, their shamans keep a ritual salve of their own making, and their battleboars are trained to viciousness. At the back of the ravine their leader, Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, keeps his own large hut, and somewhere among the quilboar dwellings lies a dirt-stained map.

title: Kodo Rock
body: Kodo Rock is a weathered stone monument on Red Cloud Mesa, standing partway along the trail from Camp Narache to Brambleblade Ravine, and it is easily missed by anyone who is not looking for it. A shaman shrine rests in its shadow, restless spirits of red stone wander the ground nearby, and battleboars from the ravine root through the grass around it. The tauren count it holy ground. Here the young shamans of Camp Narache keep the rite of earth that orc and troll shamans keep at Spirit Rock in Durotar, drinking a sapta that Seer Ravenfeather brews from a salve taken from the Bristleback shamans, and there, she promises, they will see things only their kind know of.

parts.body: Those who drink the sapta here with proper humility find the earth answering them. A manifestation of earth rises at the shrine and welcomes them, then gives a piece of rough quartz to carry back to Ravenfeather as the heart of their first totem, for even the smallest of things, it says, can outlast mountains.

title: Bloodhoof Village
body: Bloodhoof Village, named for the tribe of Cairne Bloodhoof, sits in the heart of Mulgore within the curve of Stonebull Lake. It is the first true settlement young tauren reach after leaving Red Cloud Mesa, and the busiest place on the plains outside Thunder Bluff. Cairne's son Baine is its chief, and he sends the young against the threats that trouble the land. Zarlman Two-Moons tends the spirits of the village and brews the Water of the Seers before the tribal fire, Mull Thunderhorn crafts totems to purify the wells, and the old hunter Skorn Whitecloud, old in body but fierce in spirit, still counsels young hunters. Tamed kodo are sold here as mounts, and Innkeeper Kauth welcomes every traveler.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Bloodhoof_Village (named for the Bloodhoof tribe, first settlement after Camp Narache, hub until Thunder Bluff, wild kodo tamed and sold as mounts)

title: Stonebull Lake
body: Stonebull Lake is a long, horseshoe-shaped lake that wraps around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, crossed at its narrowest point by the bridge that carries the road north toward Thunder Bluff. Its waters are rich with fish, and Uthan Stillwater teaches the angler's craft from its banks. On the northern shore the Outrunners of Mulgore fell upon a guarded Venture Company caravan and left its wagons burning, and goblins still creep back to the wreck.

parts.body: Near the village an old rancher, Ahab Wheathoof, frets over his prized puppy Kyle, who has run off again. Ahab calls for the dog and asks passersby for help, for Kyle can be coaxed home only with tender strider meat.

title: Palemane Rock
body: Palemane Rock is a cave cut into the mountains of western Mulgore, the den of the Palemane gnolls, who also make camp south of Bloodhoof Village. The gnolls tan, skin and poach the creatures of Mulgore without restraint, and they have scorned every attempt the tauren made to speak with them. For Baine Bloodhoof that disrespect was the end of patience: words, he decided, were no longer the answer. Among their camps prowls a brute called Snagglespear, and travelers who stray too close are met with snarls about fresh meat and more bones to gnaw.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Palemane_Rock (cave in western Mulgore, gnolls inside and camped outside)

title: Bael'dun Digsite
body: In the hills northwest of Bloodhoof Village, a dwarven expedition has cut a quarry into the earth at the Bael'dun Digsite. Its diggers and appraisers believe secrets lie buried in the land, and they keep histories of their own people close at hand in the camp, chronicles of the awakening of the dwarves, the War of the Three Hammers and the Battle of Grim Batol. The tauren see the dig very differently. To Baine Bloodhoof, hollowing and defiling the land is no way to earn its teachings, and the digging enrages the kodo of Mulgore. The diggers take their name from Bael'dun, the dwarven stronghold at Bael Modan in the Barrens, where the expedition is based.

title: The Sacred Wells
body: Three sacred water wells, named for the Winterhoof, Thunderhorn and Wildmane clans, give water to the people and beasts of Mulgore: Winterhoof southeast of Bloodhoof Village, Thunderhorn to its north, and Wildmane beyond Thunder Bluff. Goblins of the Venture Company, with the hirelings and laborers in their pay, have overrun all three and fouled the water with their poisons. Driving them off is not enough, for a tainted well must be cleansed. The well stones gathered around them are counted among the reagents of the Water of the Seers, and the tauren hold that the waters of Mulgore must flow clean again.
sources: quests 748, 754, 758, 760 (descriptions and reward texts: locations, goblins and their servants, cleansing)

title: The Ravaged Caravan
body: Near the northern shore of Stonebull Lake lie the burned wagons of a Venture Company caravan. It traveled under guard, and the Outrunners, who had already lost two of their number in an earlier battle with the goblins, attacked without hesitation and set it ablaze. They left the supply crates behind, trusting their torches to destroy anything of value, yet company salvagers have been seen near the wagons since, and goblin laborers and taskmasters creep back to pick over the wreckage.
sources: zone_areas 224: Venture Co. Laborer 2976, Taskmaster 2977, Sealed Supply Crate 2908

parts.body: Not every crate burned. The survivors are stamped on every side with the sign of the Venture Co. Mining Division, with notes that their contents are bound for processing at one of the company's central plants. Pried open, one proves tightly packed with ore and minerals, more evidence of goblin mining in Mulgore, with a bound sheaf of papers lying on top.

title: The Venture Co. Mine
body: The Venture Co. Mine is bored into the eastern mountains of Mulgore, northeast of the Ravaged Caravan. The goblin company was refused mining rights in the tauren homeland and dug anyway, and its workers and supervisors swarm the tunnels hauling ore from the mineral rich hills, while smoke rises from a large fire above the workings. Deep inside, Supervisor Fizsprocket oversees the whole operation.

title: The Rolling Plains
body: Southeast of Bloodhoof Village, the Rolling Plains stretch toward the mountains on Mulgore's border with the Barrens. Windfury harpies and their wind witches nest along the mountain edges away from the road, and Ruul Eagletalon of Bloodhoof sends the young against them as a gauge of their skill before they venture beyond Mulgore. The Windfuries are deadly foes whose strength in battle is matched only by their hunger for fresh meat. Prairie wolf alphas roam the grass, swoops wheel overhead, and a few Galak centaur scouts range across the eastern fields of the tauren homeland.

title: The Golden Plains
body: Southeast of Thunder Bluff opens the Golden Plains, a broad basin of grass that the tauren count among the most treasured corners of their homeland and a favored hunting ground. Plainstriders, swoops, prairie wolves and flatland cougars make it a rich country and a dangerous one. Two beasts of ill fame roam its grass: the great cat known as The Rake, and Mazzranache, a strider with demonic red eyes and a venomous bite that has been the bane of hunters for at least two generations.

title: Windfury Ridge
body: Windfury Ridge runs along the mountains of northern Mulgore, northeast of Thunder Bluff, and it belongs to the Windfury harpies. Their matriarchs and sorceresses nest along the heights and swoop down to seize or slay any traveler who strays too near, and the harpy known as Sister Hatelash hunts the northern hills not far to the west. Wolves and prowling cats roam the slopes below, and so does Arra'chea, a mighty kodo whose horn the high chieftain of Thunder Bluff accepts as proof of a young hunter's skill in tracking and the hunt.

title: Red Rocks
body: Red Rocks is a formation of red sandstone east of Thunder Bluff and the most sacred burial ground of the tauren. Only the most valiant are laid to rest there: the warriors who helped found and defend Thunder Bluff, and those who gave their lives for their tribes and chieftains. Their ancestral spirits linger among the stones, and young tauren who have drunk the Water of the Seers come here to receive their blessing. Kodo graze on the slopes around it. Lorekeeper Raintotem keeps watch over the graves, though he is too old to defend them now, and a band of Bristleback interlopers has come to ravage the burial site.
sources: quest 773 description and reward text (Ancestral Spirits, east of Thunder Bluff)

title: Baine Bloodhoof
body: Baine is the son of Cairne Bloodhoof and Tamaala, and chief of Bloodhoof Village. After the Third War, centaur led by Khiragg raided the tauren village and carried him off, and his grieving father lost the will to lead, until the wanderer Rexxar found the centaur camp and brought Baine home. Since then he has served as Cairne's adviser and leads the tribe whenever his father is away. Calm and thoughtful, he holds that the land has been good to the tauren and that respect for it is everything. He teaches that life and death are a circle, sets himself against the dwarves hollowing the western hills, and sends the young against the Palemane gnolls who slaughter Mulgore's beasts.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Baine_Bloodhoof (parents, kidnapping by Khiragg's centaur and rescue by Rexxar in Warcraft III, adviser, tribal leader when Cairne absent, calm and diplomatic)

title: The Hawkwinds
body: The Hawkwind family keeps the hearth of Camp Narache. Chief Hawkwind, an old friend of Baine Bloodhoof, has seen many eager young tauren pass through his camp and warns them that eagerness is no substitute for wisdom and experience. He sends each one toward the Rites of the Earthmother bearing a totem of his own carving, which Baine knows at a glance. His mother, Greatmother Hawkwind, still draws water from the well southeast of the camp, slower than she once was but no less devoted to the tribe, and she teaches that even the humblest task can earn the notice of elders. The chief's son Grull is a hunter who reminds the young that prey is never mere trophy.
sources: quest 747 description (Grull: my father, Chief Hawkwind)
quest 763 description and reward text (Totem of Hawkwind, my good friend)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Earlier: verified

title: Mull Thunderhorn
body: Mull Thunderhorn is a mystic of Bloodhoof Village who has taken up the cleansing of Mulgore's sacred wells since the goblins poisoned them. He cannot heal the water alone. The land itself must offer its aid, so he asks for paws, talons, claws and teeth from the creatures of the plains and, through trance and chant, binds their power into totems of cleansing. He feels every offering deeply, his spirit swelling with sadness and with pride at the sacrifice of the beasts. Goblins, he believes, will never learn the difference between contending with the land and living in harmony with it.
notes: Converted: the Thunderhorn ancestors' dream (quest 758 reward, after the second cleansing) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 758; the wells healed to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 760. 758 and 760 are tauren only (AllowableRaces 32). Earlier: verified

parts.body: As the wells begin to run clean, Mull tells of a dream in which the ancestors of the Thunderhorn clan spoke to him, praising the deed done at the well that bears their name, and in their gratitude he passes on a gift to the one who performed the ritual.

When the Wildmane well, the last and farthest, is cleansed, Mull declares the land healed and Bloodhoof Village grateful. He prays that the wind may whisper the deed for a hundred seasons, and that the waters of Mulgore remain clean forever.

title: Morin Cloudstalker
body: Morin Cloudstalker is one of the Outrunners, whose duty is to keep safe those who travel the plains of Mulgore and to punish any who threaten the tauren homeland. He keeps his post on the road east of Bloodhoof Village. After two Outrunners fell in a clash with the Venture Company, Morin's band attacked a goblin caravan near Stonebull Lake and burned it, and now that salvagers have been seen at the wreck he wants to know what its crates held. Tauren, he says, are not ones to mince words, and they have other ways of getting a message across.
sources: DB: Morin 2988 at -2369,-877, area 215, east of Bloodhoof
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Morin_Cloudstalker (on the road from Bloodhoof Village)
notes: Converted: the papers' confirmation of the plot (751 reward) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 751; Fizsprocket as mastermind and his death to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 765. The opening ends on Morin's wish to know what the crates held (749) and his own words (764 request text, kept as character). Earlier: verified

parts.body: The papers recovered from the caravan's crates confirm his fears. The Venture Company is mining Mulgore and means to rob the tauren of their natural resources, and Morin, glad at least to know it for certain, resolves that something must be done about it.

The documents also show that the company has laid many plans to drive the tauren from their land and plunder it at will, and Morin wants the mastermind behind them dead. When Supervisor Fizsprocket falls in his mine and his clipboard is brought back, Morin's anger cools a little, and he sets about searching the goblin's effects for word of what the company plans next.

title: Zarlman Two-Moons
body: Zarlman Two-Moons is the spiritual leader of Bloodhoof Village, and he always seems to sense when a young tauren walking the Rites of the Earthmother is on the way to him. He guides them through the Rite of Vision, teaching that the land is the people's most holy provider. From stones gathered at the water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath Mulgore's great trees, he brews the Water of the Seers, chanting as he mixes the reagents before the tribal fire. Those who drink it see a vision take shape before the flames, and must follow wherever it leads.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Bloodhoof_Village (Zarlman attends to the spiritual needs of the tribe)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. creature_text 3054 reread: era-neutral. Where the vision leads is told in 21526 part 2. Earlier: verified

title: Ghost Howl
body: Ghost Howl is a massive white wolf who roams the plains about the foot of Thunder Bluff. The tauren once respected him for his part in the battles against the Burning Legion, but a demon dealt him a terrible wound that never healed, and its torment has turned him against the tauren and their allies. Now he lives out his last days alone in Mulgore, his ragged hide still bearing the demon's wound.
sources: quest 770 description and reward text (wound from battles against the Burning Legion, Skorn's reaction)

Check: Opening checked against the bystander rule: who the wolf is and the wound on his hide, no outcome.

parts.body: In Bloodhoof Village the old hunter Skorn Whitecloud can scarcely believe his eyes when proof of the great wolf's death is brought to him. He looks on the hunter who did it with new respect, offers one of his own weapons for their hunts, and hopes that Ghost Howl's spirit has at last found peace.

title: Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle
body: Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle leads the Bristleback quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine, and under him the tribe wages an unending war on the tauren of Red Cloud Mesa. His raiders ambush hunting parties, steal from Camp Narache by night and train their battleboars to savagery. Sharptusk himself keeps to a large hut at the back of the ravine, in the heart of his tribe's makeshift village. Others have gone after him and failed. To the braves of the mesa he is the finest kind of quarry, one cunning enough to hunt the hunter back.
sources: quest 3376 description and request text (continued war, makeshift village, others have failed, a quarry cunning enough to hunt us back)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Brambleblade_Ravine (large hut at the back of the ravine)
notes: Converted: the siege plans moved to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 24857; Windfeather's verdict on the head to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 3376 (no KILL on the part, so group kill credit reveals nothing). The opening (KILL 8554) keeps only the war and the hunt. Earlier: verified Check: Part 1 keeps the plans vague as the Bristleback warchief's (24857 does not name Sharptusk). Opening checked against the bystander rule for KILL 8554.

parts.body: A dirt-stained map from the ravine shows how far the Bristlebacks mean to take their war. It holds plans drawn up by the Bristleback warchief for an extended siege of Camp Narache, a far greater threat than the raids the camp has endured so far.

Sharptusk's head is carried at last to Brave Windfeather on Red Cloud Mesa. Justice has been served by swift action, the brave declares, and the deed will stand as a warning to all who would threaten the tauren's home.

title: Supervisor Fizsprocket
body: Supervisor Fizsprocket runs the Venture Company's operation in Mulgore from deep inside the company mine in the eastern hills, northeast of the Ravaged Caravan. His workers and supervisors swarm the tunnels hauling ore out of the hills, though the tauren refused the company mining rights, and the Outrunners have already burned one of its guarded caravans on the shore of Stonebull Lake. Above the workings the sounds of work carry across the foothills, and smoke rises from a large fire.
sources: quest 765 description (mastermind, plans to drive us from our lands)
DB: Supervisor Fizsprocket 3051 spawn inside the Venture Co. Mine
quest 751 description (sounds of work and smoke in the foothills)
notes: Converted: the letter (page_text 352-354) moved to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT and QUEST_DONE 751; Morin naming him the mastermind to part 2 on QUEST_ACCEPT 765. The opening is unlocked by KILL 3051 (group credit), so it keeps only what anyone at the mine sees: who he is, the mine, the burned caravan. Earlier: Page text is one letter relaying Razdunk's reminder and enclosing equipment he approved; reworded. Check: Sounds of digging changed to sounds of work (quest 751 description). Opening rechecked against the bystander rule: the mine, its workers, the smoke and the burned caravan are seen on the spot, and the refused mining rights are background also given in 21511.

parts.body: Papers taken from the burned caravan are addressed to him. At President Razdunk's bidding, his superiors remind him of the company's ambitions across Kalimdor, note that its drilling and mining outposts in the Barrens already turn a profit, and press him for production numbers from Mulgore that have yet to arrive. Even so, the board has approved the equipment he requisitioned, the newest shredders and the makings of a lumber mill among it.
sources: page_text 352-354 (item 4834 Venture Co. Documents, StartItem of 751)

parts.body: Reading the documents, Morin Cloudstalker of the Outrunners names Fizsprocket the mastermind behind the company's plans to drive the tauren from their land so that it might be plundered at will. He wants the supervisor dead and his clipboard brought back for study.

title: Mazzranache
body: Mazzranache is a strider of dark reputation that stalks the Golden Plains. Maur Raincaller of Bloodhoof Village grew up on his grandfather's tales of battles with the beast: its demonic red eyes, its razor-sharp talons and its venomous bite. Crossing the plains, Maur met it himself, and it tore a nasty bite from his shoulder. Now he burns with fever and drifts into delirious nightmares, fearing the infection will be the death of him unless he can make a remedy of wolf heart, cougar femur, plainstrider scale and swoop gizzard.
sources: quest 766 description, request and reward texts
DB: Mazzranache 3068 at -1731,-541, area 820 The Golden Plains
notes: Converted: Maur's cure and his memory of the attack (766 reward text) moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 766; the opening ends on his fever and the remedy he needs (766 description and request text). The opening (KILL 3068 or ACCEPT 766) tells only Maur's tale, no outcome. Earlier: Remedy wording matched to the reward text (stops the infection, cures it in time). Faction 0 kept: Mazzranache is faction template 14, hostile to all, so the kill is open to both sides.

parts.body: With the ingredients brought to him, Maur brews a remedy that stops the spread of the infection and will cure it in time, and he owes his life to the one who gathered them. Yet he will never forget the screeching call as Mazzranache came upon him, nor the blaze of color as its beak came down.

title: Trials of Red Cloud Mesa
body: A young tauren earns a place in the tribe through deeds, and Camp Narache offers plenty. Grull Hawkwind first sends novices after plainstriders for meat and feathers, then after the mountain cougars of the southern hills, whose pelts clothe the children and mend the tents, and at last against the battleboars the Bristlebacks have trained to raid the hunting grounds, whose snouts and flanks make stew for the young. Brave Windfeather asks for something harder, the head of Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, a quarry others have failed to take. Not every trial is fought. Antur Fallow, worn out in the middle of his own Rite of Strength, begs someone to carry his father's furs down to the inn at Bloodhoof Village.
sources: quest 24857 description and reward text (started by gameobject 3076 Dirt-stained Map)
notes: Converted: the siege plans moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 24857, also an entry trigger), Hawkwind's response to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 24857), Sharptusk's head to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 3376), the furs' fate to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 1656). 24857 is the 3.3 re-id of classic quest 781 (same title and item 4850), so no era tag. Earlier: verified Check: 24857 confirmed: same text as 781, which has Flags 16384, no starter and only an ender, so it is not live and there is no double route; 24857 is QuestType 2, Flags 0, started by gameobject 3076, and OnPlayerQuestAccept fires from AddQuestAndCheckCompletion for object-started quests.

parts.body: In Brambleblade Ravine lies a dirt-stained map, and studied closely it proves to hold plans drawn up by the Bristleback warchief for an extended siege of Camp Narache. The quilboar mean to do far more than raid, and whoever finds the plans must hurry them to Chief Hawkwind.

The plans alarm Chief Hawkwind, but forewarned he can call on his brethren in Bloodhoof Village to help thwart the attack. The warning carried out of the ravine, he says, has saved the lives of many tauren.

Chief Sharptusk falls, and his head is laid before Brave Windfeather. Justice has been served by swift action, the brave declares, and the deed will stand as a warning to all who would threaten the tauren's home.

The furs reach Innkeeper Kauth sooner than he expected. They will make good blankets for any who stay at his inn, which, he says, is always open to every one of their people, for a good night's rest can make a great difference to a traveler.

title: Rites of the Earthmother
body: The Rites of the Earthmother are the steps by which a young tauren earns the respect of the elders of Thunder Bluff. They begin with a humble task, a pitcher of water carried from Greatmother Hawkwind's well southeast of Camp Narache, for even the smallest service can win an elder's notice. Three rites follow, of strength, of vision and of wisdom. For the first, Chief Hawkwind sends the youth to Seer Graytongue, whose abode is tucked into the hills south of the camp, and the Rite of Strength is a test of bravery against the Bristlebacks of Brambleblade Ravine, who ambush hunting parties and steal from the camp by dark. Beyond it the road leads down from the mesa, and in time toward Thunder Bluff itself.
notes: Converted: each rite's outcome moved out of the opening: the Rite of Strength passed and the totem for Baine to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 757), the Rite of Vision and Seer Wiserunner to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 772), the Rite of Wisdom at Red Rocks to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 773). Cairne named only as where the road leads; 775 and 776 left to Thunder Bluff. Earlier: verified

parts.body: The Rite of Strength passed, Chief Hawkwind sends the youth down the road to Bloodhoof Village with a totem of his own carving for Baine Bloodhoof, son of Cairne, who will know the carvings and help the youth along the path. Two tests remain.
sources: quest 763 description (offered by Chief Hawkwind after 757)

parts.body: In Bloodhoof the Rite of Vision begins. Zarlman Two-Moons, who always senses who walks the rites, brews the Water of the Seers from well stones and ambercorn, chanting before the tribal fire. Once it is drunk a vision takes shape before the flames, howls, and leads the youth across the plains to Seer Wiserunner, who has been expecting them and declares the Rite of Vision passed.
sources: creature_text 3054, 2983 The Plains Vision, 2984 Seer Wiserunner (ender of 772)

parts.body: The Rite of Wisdom ends at Red Rocks east of Thunder Bluff. There the ancestral spirits, the mighty tauren who gave their lives to found and protect the city, pass their duty of protection on to the young tauren, who may then enter Thunder Bluff with pride and seek out Cairne Bloodhoof atop its highest mesa.
sources: quest 773 description and reward text (Ancestral Spirit 2994)
quest 775 description (offered by the Ancestral Spirit; trigger left to Thunder Bluff)

title: The Poisoned Wells
body: When the Venture Company's goblins and their servants fouled the sacred wells of Mulgore, Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village set out to heal them, one at a time. Each well needs its own totem of cleansing, and each totem demands an offering from the land. For the Winterhoof well southeast of the village he asks the paws of prairie wolves and the talons of plainstriders. For the Thunderhorn well to the north, the claws of stalkers and cougars, whose purity in the hunt he holds vital to the work. For the Wildmane well, last and farthest, beyond Thunder Bluff, the teeth of prairie wolf alphas, a sacrifice he feels keenly. At each well the totem must be carried past the goblins and a ritual performed.
sources: quest 759 reward text (feels the sacrifice of the land)
notes: Converted: each well's cleansing moved to its own part: Winterhoof (QUEST_DONE 754), Thunderhorn (QUEST_DONE 758), Wildmane (QUEST_DONE 760). The three cleansing quests are tauren only (AllowableRaces 32), so other Horde races who take 748 see the opening alone. Earlier: verified Check: Restored Mull feeling the Wildmane sacrifice keenly (in the original, quest 759 reward text): character, not an outcome.

parts.body: The Winterhoof well is cleansed first. Word of the ritual reaches Mull moments after it is done, and already the beasts near the well drink from it eagerly. It is a great thing, he says, done for the land and for the tauren people.
The Thunderhorn well follows. The ancestors of the Thunderhorn clan speak to Mull in a dream, praising the one who cleansed the well that bears their name, and they send a gift in their gratitude.

Last of all the Wildmane well north of Thunder Bluff is purified, and the goblins' poisons are gone from all three. Mull declares the land healed and Bloodhoof Village grateful, and prays that the wind will whisper the deed for a hundred seasons and the waters of Mulgore remain clean forever.

title: The Venture Company in Mulgore
body: The Outrunners had already lost two of their own to the Venture Company when they found a goblin caravan traveling under guard on the northern shore of Stonebull Lake. They fell on it at once and burned it, leaving the supply crates behind in the belief that their torches had destroyed anything of value. But company salvagers have since been seen picking through the wreck, and Morin Cloudstalker, who keeps the Outrunners' watch on the road east of Bloodhoof Village, wants someone to go and look inside the crates. If the goblins mean to exploit the tauren homeland as they have exploited other lands, the Outrunners will put an end to it.
notes: Converted: the crates' contents moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 749, QUEST_ACCEPT 751), the documents and Morin's verdict to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 751), the strike on the mine to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 764), Fizsprocket as mastermind and his death to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 765). 764 and 765 both follow 751 and can be done in either order; each part stands on its own trigger. Earlier: Documents reworded (one letter, equipment approved by Razdunk). Check: Part 2 wording matched to page_text 352. Parts 3 (764) and 4 (765) each read on from part 2 alone, so either order works.

parts.body: Some crates survived the fire. Each is stamped with the sign of the Venture Co. Mining Division and marked for processing at one of the company's central plants, and inside lie ore and minerals packed tight, with a sheaf of papers on top. Up in the foothills to the east, the sounds of work carry on the wind and smoke rises from a large fire.

The papers are a letter to Supervisor Fizsprocket, enclosing a list of equipment approved by President Razdunk, urging greater production from the mineral rich plains and promising shredders and a lumber mill besides. To Morin they prove that the company means to rob the tauren of their natural resources, and he resolves that something must be done.

The company had been refused mining rights in Mulgore and dug anyway, so Morin sends the goblins a message in the tauren way. Workers and supervisors are struck down in the mine northeast of the caravan, a signal, Morin judges, that no goblin could misread: the tauren will not let their land be robbed without protest.
sources: quest 764 description, request and reward texts

parts.body: The documents also lay bare the company's plans to drive the tauren from their land so that it might be plundered at will, and the mastermind behind them is Supervisor Fizsprocket. He is slain in his mine and his clipboard carried back to Morin, who means to search it for whatever the Venture Company has planned next.

title: Sharing the Land
body: Baine Bloodhoof teaches that the land has been good to the tauren and must be respected in return, and two intruders in Mulgore have refused that lesson. To the south and west, the Palemane gnolls kill the creatures of the plains without restraint and have scorned every attempt to speak with them, so Baine sends the young to cut down their tanners, skinners and poachers, so that they may see how terrible even a small threat to the land can become if left unchecked. To the northwest, dwarves are hollowing the hills at the Bael'dun Digsite in search of the earth's secrets, and their digging enrages the kodo. There Baine asks not for blood but for their tools: picks taken from the dig and smashed at a forge.
sources: quest 745 description, request and reward texts
quest 746 description, request and reward texts
notes: Converted: Baine's words on each turn-in moved to parts: the circle of death and life to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 745), the hope for the dwarves to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 746). 745 and 746 run side by side, so either part can come first. Earlier: verified Check: Part 1 now has Baine remind the young of the circle, so it agrees with 21516, whose opening gives the circle as his standing teaching (a maxim, not an outcome).

parts.body: When the Palemane hunters have fallen, Baine is glad the task was taken seriously. Had the gnolls respected the land and its creatures, he says, the conflict would never have come. Death and life, he reminds them, are a circle and a necessity, and neither can exist without the other: a lesson he asks the young never to forget.
The broken tools brought back from the dig will calm the beasts of Mulgore, Baine says, and, spirits willing, they will teach the dwarves that hollowing the land is not the path to knowledge.
